title: Joining Streams: merge, concat, zip, forkJoin, and race

questions.prompt: Which operator behaves most like `Promise.all` — waiting for all sources to complete, then emitting each source's final value once?

options.text: forkJoin
merge
zip
race

questions.explanation: forkJoin waits for every source to complete, then emits a single array/object of the last value from each. It errors if any source errors — exactly like Promise.all.

options.text: 'later' never runs, because interval never completes
'later' emits immediately, before the interval
Both run concurrently and interleave
It errors on subscription

questions.explanation: concat only moves to the next source after the current one completes. interval never completes, so 'later' never starts. Use merge if order doesn't matter, or bound the interval with take.

options.text: By index — it pairs a's n-th value with b's n-th value into a tuple
By latest — it re-emits whenever either source changes
By interleaving them as they arrive
By taking only the first source to emit

questions.explanation: zip is positional: it emits [a0, b0], [a1, b1], … waiting until both have the n-th value. Surplus values from a faster source are buffered.

questions.prompt: `race(a$, b$)` — b$ emits its first value before a$. What does race do?

options.text: Mirrors b$ and unsubscribes from a$
Emits values from both, interleaved
Waits for both to complete then emits the last of each
Mirrors a$ because it was listed first

questions.explanation: race picks the first source to emit (b$) as the winner, mirrors it, and cancels the losers.

questions.prompt: Which operators require their sources to COMPLETE to behave correctly? Select all that apply.

options.text: forkJoin — needs every source to complete to emit at all
concat — needs each source to complete before the next starts
merge — emits values as they arrive regardless of completion
race — needs all sources to complete before choosing a winner

questions.explanation: forkJoin waits for all completions; concat depends on each source completing to advance. merge emits immediately and race decides on the first emission — neither needs completion to produce values.

questions.prompt: Match each joining operator to its behaviour.

pairs.right: Run sources one after another, in order
Pair values by index into tuples
Mirror the first source to emit

questions.explanation: merge interleaves, concat sequences, zip pairs positionally, and race picks the first responder.
